Strocon's industrial installations are used, among other things, in biogas plants, where organic waste streams such as potatoes, bread, carrots and other food residues are processed into energy or reused as sustainable animal feed. In these processes, every deviation has a direct impact on production capacity, energy consumption and efficiency.

Operators must be able to immediately recognize deviations, understand the underlying cause, and intervene in a timely manner. Without a complete and real-time overview, it takes a great deal of time to establish connections between various process variables, resulting in missed optimization opportunities and plants consuming energy unnecessarily or operating below their maximum capacity.
To provide operators with faster insight into their processes and to

Important process parameters, such as plant filling time, humidity and temperature differences during the drying process, are visible in real time. This allows operators to intervene immediately when a process deviates, prevent energy loss and
maximize the efficiency of the plant

When processing coarse materials, operators analyze how efficiently the crane functions. They see in real time how long the crane runs automatically, when it stops and how much product is moved per cycle. Based on these insights, settings, such as the crane's recipe, can be adjusted to achieve the desired filling level. This ensures a more efficient process and a higher processing capacity.

The drying process is also continuously monitored. Operators monitor, among other things, humidity, temperature differences (Delta T) and the utilization of the drying air. When deviations occur, for example because the product layer is unevenly distributed across the drying belt, they can intervene immediately to prevent energy loss and ensure consistent product quality.
